questiontext.text:
Consider the trigonometric equation \( {@eqn@}, \qquad 0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ. \)

Give all angles in degrees, as exact whole numbers.

(a) Determine the reference angle \(\alpha\) for the equation.

\(\alpha = \) [[input:ans0]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans0]] [[feedback:prt0]]

(b) In which quadrants do the solutions lie? Tick all that apply.

[[input:ans_ref]] [[validation:ans_ref]] [[feedback:prtq]]

(c) Hence solve the equation for \(0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ\).

First solution: \(\theta = \) [[input:ans1]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
Second solution: \(\theta = \) [[input:ans2]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We are solving \({@eqn@}\) for \(0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ\).

[[if test="is(m>1)"]]

Step 0: get \(\tan\theta\) on its own. Divide both sides by \({@m@}\):

\[ \tan\theta = \frac{ {@rhs@} }{ {@m@} } = {@k@}. \][[/if]]

(a) Step 1: determine the reference angle.

The reference angle \(\alpha\) is the acute angle whose tangent is the size of \(\tan\theta\), ignoring the sign. From the special triangles, \(\tan {@alpha@}^\circ = [[if test="is(idx=1)"]]\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[[/if]][[if test="is(idx=2)"]]1[[/if]][[if test="is(idx=3)"]]\sqrt{3}[[/if]]\), so

\[ \alpha = {@alpha@}^\circ. \]

(b) Step 2: identify the quadrants.

\(\tan\theta = {@k@}\) is [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]positive. By the CAST rule, tangent is positive in Quadrant I (All) and Quadrant III (Tangent)[[else]]negative. By the CAST rule, tangent is positive only in Quadrants I and III, so it is negative in Quadrants II and IV[[/if]]. There is one solution in each of these quadrants.

(c) Step 3: find the solution in each quadrant.

    [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]
  • Quadrant I: the angle equals the reference angle, \(\theta_1 = \alpha = {@alpha@}^\circ\).
  • Quadrant III: go \(\alpha\) past \(180^\circ\), \(\theta_2 = 180^\circ + \alpha = 180^\circ + {@alpha@}^\circ = {@ta2@}^\circ\).
    • [[else]]
  • Quadrant II: stop \(\alpha\) short of \(180^\circ\), \(\theta_1 = 180^\circ - \alpha = 180^\circ - {@alpha@}^\circ = {@ta1@}^\circ\).
  • Quadrant IV: stop \(\alpha\) short of \(360^\circ\), \(\theta_2 = 360^\circ - \alpha = 360^\circ - {@alpha@}^\circ = {@ta2@}^\circ\).
    • [[/if]]

Step 4: check the range. Both angles lie in \(0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ\). Notice that \({@ta2@}^\circ - {@ta1@}^\circ = 180^\circ\): the solutions of a tangent equation are always \(180^\circ\) apart. [[if test="is(sg=-1)"]]A calculator gives \(\tan^{-1}\left({@k@}\right) = -{@alpha@}^\circ\), which is outside the range; adding \(180^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\) gives the two solutions.[[/if]]

Final answer:

\[ \theta = {@ta1@}^\circ \quad\text{or}\quad \theta = {@ta2@}^\circ. \]

Seeing the solutions. On the graph of \(y = \tan\theta\) (with asymptotes at \(90^\circ\) and \(270^\circ\), where \(\tan\theta\) is undefined), the line \(y = {@k@}\) crosses the curve exactly twice in the range:
